messages.subject: model formulation
parts:
Dear breedR users,

I am coming with simple question concerning to model formulation. 
Lets consider the example

res.blk <- remlf90(fixed  = phe_X ~ gg,
                   genetic = gen.globulus, 
                   spatial = list(model = 'blocks', 
                                  coord = globulus[, c('x','y')],
                                  id = 'bl'),
                   data = globulus)

Assuming that there is no genetic group in studied material, what will be the right way to write the model in breedR?

Could I use 1 instead gg?

Jan

messages.author: 37c4b6bc71d5d203
messages.subject: Re: [breedR] model formulation
parts:
Hi Jan!

Yes, you put `1` instead of `gg` to just fit a global mean.

You will also want to define `gen.globulus` appropriately. Do you have a pedigree, or maybe families?
